key_insight: PRET uses a few example slides to recognize cancers across organs, hospitals and tasks without task-specific training; it targets pathology recognition, not drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The system could help scale AI-assisted pathology where labeled data and pathologists are scarce, but the reported results do not establish readiness for routine clinical use.
method: Few-shot pan-cancer recognition using example slides.
No task-specific training on those examples.
Evaluated across organs, hospitals and recognition tasks.
evidence_signal: Across 23 international benchmarks containing 4,484 whole-slide images, PRET outperformed existing approaches on 20 tasks and achieved over 97% AUC on 15 benchmarks; with eight example slides, it also outperformed 11 pathologists in a lymph node metastasis evaluation.
watch_item: Prospective validation in real-world clinical workflows is needed before assuming these benchmark results generalize to routine care.
paper_title: PRET is a few-shot system for pan-cancer recognition without example training
